guideline: CPIC Guideline for CYP2D6 and CYP2C19 Genotypes and Dosing of Tricyclic Antidepressants: 2016 Update (Hicks JK, Sangkuhl K, Swen JJ, Ellingrod VL, Müller DJ, Shimoda K, Bishop JR, Kharasch ED, Skaar TC, Gaedigk A, Dunnenberger HM, Klein TE, Caudle KE, Stingl JC). Clin Pharmacol Ther. 2017 Jul;102(1):37-44. doi:10.1002/cpt.597. Published July 2017 (the "2016 update"; supersedes the 2013 guideline). Recommendations below are transcribed from Table 2 (CYP2D6), Table 3 (CYP2C19, tertiary amines) and Table 4 (combined, amitriptyline).

recommendations.text: Avoid tricyclic use due to potential lack of efficacy. Consider alternative drug not metabolized by CYP2D6. If a TCA is warranted, consider titrating to a higher target dose (compared to normal metabolizers); titrate to observed clinical response. Utilize therapeutic drug monitoring to guide dose adjustments.
recommendations.citation: CPIC TCA guideline 2016 update (Hicks et al., Clin Pharmacol Ther 2017;102(1):37-44), Table 2. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5478479/

notes:
SOURCE: All rows transcribed from the full text of the guideline PDF (files.cpicpgx.org/data/guideline/publication/TCA/2016/TCA_2016.pdf), cross-checked against the PMC copy (PMC5478479). Note the naming: the paper is titled the "2016 update" but was published July 2017 in Clin Pharmacol Ther 102(1):37-44 — these are ONE document, not two. There is no separate "2017 update"; the only thing dated 2017 is the issue date of the same 2016-update guideline. If the prototype expects two distinct guideline versions, that expectation is wrong. (CPIC has since re-hosted its guideline pages on clinpgx.org; cpicpgx.org URLs 302-redirect there.)

GENE COVERAGE — CYP2D6-only vs both genes:
- CYP2D6 ONLY (secondary amines): nortriptyline, desipramine. CPIC states "TCAs without major CYP2C19 metabolism include the secondary amines nortriptyline and desipramine," and Table 3 explicitly covers only tertiary amines. I did NOT create CYP2C19 rows for nortriptyline or desipramine — CPIC gives no CYP2C19 recommendation for them. The lookup table should return "no CYP2C19 recommendation" for those two rather than defaulting to "standard".
- BOTH CYP2D6 + CYP2C19 (tertiary amines): amitriptyline, clomipramine, doxepin, imipramine, trimipramine.

PHENOTYPE GAP — CYP2D6 "Rapid Metabolizer" does not exist in this guideline. Table 1 defines only CYP2D6 ultrarapid (activity score >2.0), normal (1.0-2.0), intermediate (0.5) and poor (0). "Rapid metabolizer" is a CYP2C19-only category (one normal + one increased-function allele, e.g. *1/*17). I included explicit no_recommendation rows for CYP2D6 Rapid so the prototype has a deterministic "no rule" hit instead of an empty lookup that an LLM might fill in.

STALENESS WARNING on the activity-score cutoffs: the phenotype definitions in this 2016/2017 guideline predate CPIC's 2019 standardized phenotype consensus (Caudle et al., Clin Transl Sci 2020) and the 2019 CYP2D6 activity-score revision, which reassigned activity score 1.0 from normal to INTERMEDIATE metabolizer and changed the *1/*10-type assignments. The recommendation text per phenotype is unchanged, but genotype-to-phenotype translation should come from the current CPIC CYP2D6 allele/phenotype tables, not from Table 1 of this paper. I have not independently verified the current translation tables here — if the prototype does genotype-to-phenotype mapping, that is a separate lookup that needs its own sourcing.

EVIDENCE TIERS (why the same text carries different strengths): CPIC gives two classification columns per table. Table 2 (CYP2D6) rates amitriptyline + nortriptyline separately from "other TCAs"; Table 3 (CYP2C19) rates amitriptyline separately from "other tertiary amine TCAs". The evidence base is amitriptyline/nortriptyline; the rest is extrapolation on pharmacokinetic similarity, which is why nearly every non-amitriptyline/nortriptyline row is Optional. Exception: normal metabolizers are Strong across all drugs in both tables. I encoded this in the `strength` field and flagged extrapolated rows in `citation`.

DOSE PERCENTAGES — only three numeric adjustments exist in the whole guideline:
- CYP2D6 intermediate: 25% reduction of recommended starting dose.
- CYP2D6 poor: 50% reduction (only if a TCA is used at all — the primary advice is avoid).
- CYP2C19 poor: 50% reduction of recommended starting dose for tertiary amines.
No percentage is given for CYP2D6 ultrarapid: CPIC says there are "insufficient data in the literature to calculate a starting dose" and to titrate upward under TDM. Do not surface a number there. "Starting dose" throughout means the recommended STEADY-STATE dose, not the day-1 dose — patients may begin lower and titrate up over several days. A prototype that applies 25%/50% to a literal day-1 dose is misreading the guideline.

THERAPEUTIC DRUG MONITORING (the prototype surfaces this — verbatim points):
- TDM is attached to every non-normal phenotype recommendation: CYP2D6 UM, IM and PM, and CYP2C19 UM/RM and PM all carry "utilize therapeutic drug monitoring to guide dose adjustments."
- For CYP2D6 ultrarapid specifically, TDM is "strongly recommended" because no starting dose can be calculated.
- Combined-genotype rule (Table 4, footnote f): "Utilizing therapeutic drug monitoring if a tricyclic is prescribed to a patient with CYP2D6 ultrarapid, intermediate, or poor metabolism in combination with CYP2C19 ultrarapid, intermediate, or poor metabolism is strongly recommended." The body text adds CYP2C19 rapid to that list.
- Rationale CPIC gives: TCA plasma concentrations are predictive of toxicity and efficacy and therapeutic ranges are defined; poor and ultrarapid metabolizers may fall outside the range. CPIC also notes genotype correlates better with plasma concentration than with clinical response — studies conflict — so TDM is the bridge, not a replacement for clinical judgment.
- Dose titration guidance paired with TDM: "titrate dose to observed clinical response with symptom improvement and minimal (if any) side effects."

COMBINED CYP2D6 + CYP2C19 (Table 4, amitriptyline) — NOT expressible in this flat one-gene-per-row schema, so I am recording it here in full. It is not a simple AND of the single-gene rows and the prototype will get combined cases wrong if it just intersects them. Grid is CYP2C19 phenotype (row) x CYP2D6 phenotype (column):
- C19 UM or RM: with D6 UM -> avoid amitriptyline (Optional). D6 NM -> consider alternative not metabolized by CYP2C19 (Optional). D6 IM -> consider alternative not metabolized by CYP2C19 (Optional). D6 PM -> avoid amitriptyline (Optional).
- C19 NM: D6 UM -> avoid; if warranted consider titrating to a higher target dose (Strong). D6 NM -> recommended starting dose (Strong). D6 IM -> 25% reduction (Moderate). D6 PM -> avoid; if warranted 50% reduction (Strong).
- C19 IM: D6 UM -> avoid (Optional). D6 NM -> recommended starting dose (Strong). D6 IM -> 25% reduction (Optional). D6 PM -> avoid; if warranted 50% reduction (Optional).
- C19 PM: D6 UM -> avoid (Optional). D6 NM -> avoid; if warranted 50% reduction (Moderate). D6 IM -> avoid (Optional). D6 PM -> avoid (Optional).
Note the asymmetry worth encoding: C19 IM + D6 NM is Strong "standard dose", but C19 PM + D6 NM drops to "avoid / 50% reduction". Table 4 is amitriptyline-specific; CPIC says extrapolating it to clomipramine, doxepin, imipramine and trimipramine is reasonable but the classification of that extrapolation is Optional. I did not extrapolate Table 4 into rows myself.

SCOPE LIMIT the prototype must enforce: every dose recommendation above "only appl[ies] to higher initial doses of TCAs for treatment of conditions such as depression." For NEUROPATHIC PAIN, where amitriptyline is dosed lower (CPIC cites ~0.1 mg/kg/day in pediatrics, 25 mg daily initial in adults), CPIC recommends NO dose modification for poor or intermediate metabolizers, with close monitoring for side effects; the gene-based tables apply only if larger doses are warranted. CPIC also states there are limited data for CYP2C19*17 carriers on low-dose amitriptyline for neuropathic pain. Surfacing a 25%/50% reduction to a neuropathic-pain prescriber would be a misapplication of this guideline.

WHAT I DID NOT CONFIRM: I did not retrieve the Supplementary Data, so the formal definitions of the Strong/Moderate/Optional rating scheme and the supplemental evidence tables (S5-S16) are cited but not verified verbatim. I also did not check PharmGKB/ClinPGx for any post-2017 CPIC errata or the current clinpgx.org rendering of these tables; if the prototype ships clinically, that check should be done against clinpgx.org/guideline/PA166251445. Population phenotype frequencies from Table 1 (e.g. CYP2D6 PM ~1-10%) were read from a summarizing fetch rather than the raw PDF and are not included in the matrix — do not surface frequencies from this dataset.
